summary: An inherited review-wait ledger was unretirable by construction, and the recovery route that creates the wedge is the same one required to take the item over. The wait entry's claimGeneration named a claim-marker comment that no longer existed, and ReviewWait.project compares the STORED receipt's generation against the LIVE claim - so timeout, cancel and complete were all refused with 'entry receipt claimGeneration is not current' regardless of which generation the event supplied, while a fresh enter was refused with 'a preceding reviewGeneration is still unconsumed'. The trap is that a dead holder can only be displaced by claim --force, which mints a new generation and thereby guarantees the mismatch: any inheriting worker converts a merely-expired wait into an unretirable one by the act of inheriting it. Recovery required preserving the entry verbatim and deleting it. Recorded because the before/after oracle pair is the only thing that distinguishes this from a false exhaustion.

A committed gate-inversion harness that nothing invokes is a record, not a gate - the exact failure its own header warns about. scripts/test-working-set-gate-mutations.sh shipped referenced by zero call sites while the repository's equivalent, scripts/test-spatial-subject-mutations.sh, has three. The proof that three new fixtures can fail therefore ran once, by hand, and would not have re-run when a later refactor reshaped the literals the mutations match - which is precisely how a mutation harness goes vacuous. Wired into verify-spatial-query.sh's serial direct route; NOT into the concurrent prepared-PR route, because unlike the existing harness this one mutates sources in the working tree rather than in an isolated mutant directory, so the CI route needs that isolation first.

Performance evidence measured against a base that has moved is not evidence about the change any more. This item's before/after table was taken against a main 62 commits older; re-measured after rebasing, F4's win moved from 3.5x to 2.9x and F3 went from 'no change' to 5% slower. The ratios that mattered survived, but one headline number did not, and carrying the old table forward would have overstated a win by 20% while the structural counters - identical in all three rounds on both sides - were the part actually worth quoting. Timings were restated with their spread and explicitly marked unstable; the counters were marked stable.
